```{r}
#| include: false
source("../../../assets/theme_StellarGrok.R")
library(ggplot2)
```

R ships with a dataset of daily air quality readings from New York, May to September 1973.
It's small, a bit messy, and a great excuse to show off the blog's ggplot theme.

```{r}
aq <- airquality
aq$Month <- factor(month.abb[aq$Month], levels = month.abb[5:9])
knitr::kable(head(aq), caption = "First six rows")
```

## Ozone climbs through the summer

```{r}
#| label: fig-ozone
#| fig-cap: "Daily ozone by month. July and August run hottest."
#| warning: false
ggplot(aq, aes(Month, Ozone, fill = Month)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, colour = fn_cols[["forest"]], alpha = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_StellarGrok() +
  labs(title = "Ozone peaks in mid-summer", x = NULL, y = "Ozone (ppb)",
       caption = "Source: R datasets::airquality")
```

## Temperature explains a lot of it

```{r}
#| label: fig-temp
#| fig-cap: "Ozone against temperature with a loess smoother."
#| warning: false
#| message: false
ggplot(aq, aes(Temp, Ozone)) +
  geom_point(colour = fn_cols[["forest_500"]], alpha = 0.7, size = 2.4) +
  geom_smooth(colour = fn_cols[["pink"]], fill = fn_cols[["sage_200"]], linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Hotter days, more ozone", x = "Temperature (°F)", y = "Ozone (ppb)")
```

::: {.callout-note}
About a quarter of the ozone readings are missing. `ggplot2` drops them quietly, which is
fine for a sketch but worth handling properly in real work.
:::
